explanation: No clear shared feature: fires on assorted tokens in boilerplate web text ('You will [hear] from us'), C #include headers ('.h'), code comment openers ('/**', ' *'), metadata labels ('Category:'), and mid-word subword pieces of technical/scientific terms ('ocyte', 'ro', 'erm', 'pan'). Activations are mostly moderate apart from one outlier.

Fires on programming identifiers and API/class names in code or technical Q&A, especially CamelCase identifiers or their continuation pieces (ClassName, JsonObject, IllegalArgumentException, marginTop, ObjectContext, DataTable) and '.googleapis' in Google URLs. Weak to none on ordinary prose words.

Fires strongly on the '.S' in the legal citation 'U.S.C.' (e.g. '28 U.S.C. §'), and also on path/structure tokens in code and URLs ('/' in blog URLs, 'docs' in 'httpdocs', '//' comment lines, '/core', 'frame' in \end{frame}), plus a scattering of unrelated prose words (officer, component, piqued).

Fires on a variable or argument token in mathematical or technical notation, strongest on the opening of a function call argument in algebra problems ('v*b[(j]', 'y[(b]'), and on 'a predetermined/defined/parameter' style terms naming a quantity in technical or patent prose. Also fires on assorted math symbols and the date line ending court headers.

A mixture: runs of zeros in numbers ('0000000'), the subword 'oid' in 'rheumatoid', 'ulla' in 'medulla', pieces of CJK/Vietnamese characters, and code tokens in import/path statements (tkinter import, os.path, localhost, __init__). No single shared feature.

Fires on a token inside a title or name that repeats a phrase already given earlier in the document, typically the second mention of a headline/entity name right after the title (e.g. 'Carabus albrechti awashim[ae]', 'McLeod's Da[ughters]', the second COVID in a duplicated headline, repeated #define guard names). Strength depends on the context copying earlier text, not the token itself.

Fires on the word that completes a fixed multiword phrase: 'nothing/little to [do] with', 'granted in [part]', 'relates [generally] to' in patent openings, 'in favor [of]', 'worry [about]'. Also fires weakly on numbers in diff hunk headers and UUIDs. Mostly one idea, phrase completion, with some noise.

Fires on a token inside a domain-specific technical compound term, often a subword in the middle of medical/scientific words ('hypoth[al]amic', 'polyc[yst]ic', 'thromboc[yt]openia', 'root [plan]ing', 'gall[stone]') or a jargon piece in code/legal text ('$[schema]', 'layout[_width]', 'assign]ee'). This is a broad 'continuation of a specialized term' feature with a noisy edge.

Fires on a token in the middle or end of a proper name or specialized term, where the earlier tokens predict it: 'Bureau [of] Investigation', 'United States [Navy]', 'epidermolysis bul[los]a', 'Harry [Potter]', 'Voivodes[hip]', and the '-' list item after 'bibliography:' in YAML. A broad 'complete the multi-token entity' feature without one clear topic.

Fires on the first subword piece of a word that is split into several tokens, especially word-initial fragments like 'St' (Stroop, Stammer, St.), 'sh' (shivers, shudder), single capital letters starting a word, and the first byte of multibyte CJK characters. Fires across many languages; it is about starting a word fragment, not meaning.

Diffuse: fires on function words and operators that sit between two parts of a structured expression ('look [at]', 'not counting [the]', '[+]' in arithmetic, ',' between template params, '(P' in p-values, indentation in code). No clear single trigger.

Fires on the second word of fixed vague or indefinite constructions: 'of' in 'some kind/type of', 'not' in 'whether or not', 'way' in 'in some/whatever/every way'. Moderate on other 'way'/'to' continuations.

Fires on a connective joining two parallel items or giving an example, especially 'or' after an adverb ('gradually or', 'individually or', 'rarely or'), 'and' in 'Individually and as', 'such as', 'also' in 'not only... but also', and 'is' after 'one way to X'. Ties to coordination and comparison inside a phrase.

Fires on structural tokens in code and code-license headers: '~' of C++ destructors (strongest), 'information'/'view'/'found' in standard license boilerplate, '0' in for-loop initializers, 'public:', '||', '|' in types. Only appears in source-code contexts, but the jobs within it differ.
